hints: Think about the last character of src and of dst. If they already match, do you need to touch them? If not, what are the three things the last step could have been?
2D DP over prefixes: dp[i][j] = fewest steps to turn the first i letters of src into the first j letters of dst. Insert, delete and overwrite each map to one neighbouring cell.

1. Base cases: dp[i][0] = i (delete everything) and dp[0][j] = j (insert everything).
  2. For each i, j: if src[i-1] == dst[j-1], dp[i][j] = dp[i-1][j-1].
  3. Else dp[i][j] = 1 + min(dp[i-1][j-1] (overwrite), dp[i-1][j] (delete), dp[i][j-1] (insert)).
  4. Return dp[n][m]; two rolling rows are enough.

approaches.name: Brute force
approaches.idea: Recursively try all three operations at every mismatch without caching.

approaches.name: Optimal
approaches.idea: Bottom-up prefix DP with two rows.

explain: For "kitten" → "sitting": the first row and column count pure inserts/deletes. The cell for k vs s costs 1 (overwrite); later the itt parts match for free along the diagonal; e vs i costs another overwrite, and the final g is one insert, total 3. Each cell is correct because the last action on the prefixes must be one of the three operations (or a free match). Edge case: an empty src or dst — the base row/column already gives the length of the other string, like 3 for "" → "abc".
recognize: 'Turn string A into string B with insert / delete / replace, minimum steps' → edit-distance DP over prefixes.
